rated_messages.input_message: Take a minute to notice what the urge feels like in your body without smoking a cigarette. Notice what is going on. See what happens. Does the urge pass?

If you get any urges tonight, why not confront them head on? Ask the urge - what's it going to give you? It's not going to make you richer, or better looking, and it's not going to leave you if you give in either!
Take a deep breath and let it out slowly. Notice that you are completely OK for this one breath. Do it again.
Tell yourself, “I am going to quit smoking soon.” Say it out loud. Say to yourself, “I am too strong to continue smoking for the rest of my life."

When smoking, it can feel like your hands are for holding a cigarette, your mouth is for smoking the cigarette, and your chest and lungs need to breathe in the smoke. Spend 3 minutes noticing how your hands feel, how your mouth feels, and how your chest feels. The more you practice noticing these things without smoking, the sooner your body will stop being a trigger for you.
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
Are you feeling down because you are thinking of smoking? It's really important to be kind to yourself, and to make sure you give yourself praise too!
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.
When a craving hits, keep your hands busy by doing the dishes or taking out the trash. Small chores will help pass the time during a craving.
Ask yourself, "From 0-10, how willing am I to let this urge pass without smoking?" Let it pass to be closer to the things that matter most to you.
